messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 2938000123 — solstice-enterprises (dedicated VPC us-west-2): elevated egress error rate observed. External client TLS handshakes failing, 502/504 spikes. Auto-pager triggered.

Alice M.: paging @Dinesh (oncall) — are you live? this looks like customer-dedicated pool only.

Dinesh (OnCall): on it, joining. any blast radius details? single tenant or shared pool?

Ben (Network): telemetry shows TCP RSTs from NLBs bound to Solstice pool starting ~10:02 UTC, healthchecks still green for internal targets but upstream TLS handshakes timeout.

Carla (SRE): quick check — is this the dedicated pool with private subnets + egress NATGW? could be NAT saturation or SG rule flap.

Ellis (Support): Sam (Solstice) reporting ~30% request failures from their customers, started ~10:01 UTC. They see intermittent connection resets.

Sam Patel - Solstice: confirming, both our API and webhook deliveries failing intermittently. We have retries but customers notice latency. Any ETA on mitigation?

Dinesh (OnCall): OK. isolating: i) confirm only Solstice tenant impacted ii) gather NLB/ALB target health and SG changes iii) check NATGW CloudWatch metrics.

Ben (Network): running quick checks — target groups show healthy targets, but NLB connections show high active flows and increased SYN-ACK retransmits. NATGW connections at 100% for one AZ.

Carla (SRE): that smells like ephemeral port exhaustion on NAT or conntrack limits on egress proxies. can we see conntrack/sysstat on the egress instances?

Dinesh (OnCall): grabbing SSH to egress bastion.

Ben (Network): logs from the edge show repeated "connection reset by peer" to the upstream client IPs. Also noticed security-group update pushed ~09:58 UTC in that tenant's onboarding automation — maybe a rollback race?

Alice M.: @Carla recall any recent infra rollouts that could touch sg rules in us-west-2?

Carla (SRE): we had a patch that tightened ephemeral port egress rules last night but it was behind a feature flag and only targeted shared pools. Not supposed to touch dedicated pools. I'll check audit logs.

Ellis (Support): Sam, can you confirm if you deployed anything around 10:00 UTC on your side?

Sam Patel - Solstice: no deploys from us. Only normal traffic. We turned up some synthetic checks at 09:50 UTC but nothing that would alter infra.

Dinesh (OnCall): action plan: 1) fail traffic off the saturated NATGW to standby egress (traffic-split) 2) temporarily increase NATGW capacity in affected AZ 3) rollback any recent SG change if found 4) set DNS weight to drain to healthy region if needed. I'm going to open a short-lived traffic split.

Ben (Network): preparing weighted routing change. will move 30% traffic to us-west-1 standby for Solstice. keeping TTL low (30s).

Carla (SRE): i'm checking customer-side SG audit: 09:58 change was to add a monitoring CIDR, it shouldn't block egress. but the automation incorrectly applied a null rule to the egress group for one interface — i'm seeing a replace event. rolling that back now.

Dinesh (OnCall): executing egress split. Ben, can you confirm the Route53 weighted record ID?

Ben (Network): confirming: route53 hosted zone Z123SOL, record solstice-api.prod.redwood.example. Changing weights now to 70/30 us-west-2/us-west-1. TTL=30s.

inc-bot: :white_check_mark: Route53 change submitted by Ben (Network).

Ben (Network): applied. monitoring traffic shift.

Carla (SRE): rollback of SG null rule completed. re-evaluating conntrack on egress instances.

Dinesh (OnCall): increasing NATGW throughput—spawning additional NATGWs in the affected AZ and attaching to the private route table for the Solstice subnets.

Ellis (Support): Sam, you're seeing any improvement on the Solstice side after the split?

Sam Patel - Solstice: initial dashboards look marginally better, error rate dropping from 30% -> ~12% after ~2 minutes. webhooks still have some retries but fewer.

Carla (SRE): conntrack on egress instance before rollback: 490k entries, conntrack-max 524k. after SG rollback and NATGW add, entries dropping to 210k. looks like many half-closed sockets were accumulating.

Dinesh (OnCall): good. next steps: 1) keep weights for 15 minutes while we validate stability 2) provision permanent extra NATGW or enable autoscale for this customer pool 3) root cause: investigate client-side retries + earlier SG misapplication causing half-open sessions.

Ben (Network): metrics: upstream TLS handshakes recovered from 40% fail -> 5% fail after the split. NLB connection queueing reduced.

Ellis (Support): I'm updating the customer: "We've shifted some traffic and added capacity; error rates are falling. We'll keep monitoring and follow up with RCA."

Sam Patel - Solstice: thanks — please keep us posted. can we get a postmortem with timeline and suggest guardrails?

Carla (SRE): noted. I'll own the RCA with network and infra. preliminary cause: automation bug that inserted an empty SG rule combined with NATGW peak causing connections to accumulate.

Dinesh (OnCall): handing off to @Carla for next 2 hours for RCA and follow-through. I'm going offline for scheduled meeting but will be available if paging escalates. taking the incident to SEV-2 -> monitoring.

Carla (SRE): taking over. next: 1) confirm autoscale policy for NATGW in dedicated pools 2) add preflight check to automation to avoid null-rule application 3) coordinate with Solstice on connection retry/backoff guidance.

inc-bot: :information_source: Incident 2938000123 status changed to MONITORING. Lead: Carla (SRE). Severity: SEV-2. Started: 2938000123.

Alice M.: thumbs up — great quick mitigation. please file postmortem and link runbook updates.

Ben (Network): I'll keep the weighted routing in place until Carla gives the all-clear, will set TTL back to 300s after stability window.

Sam Patel - Solstice: appreciate the rapid response. keep me in the loop for RCA and any config changes we need to make.

Ellis (Support): updating support ticket and customer comms. next update at +30m or earlier if status changes.

Carla (SRE): noted, collecting logs and audit trail now. I'll post a summary and action items once complete.

Dinesh (OnCall): thanks team, handing over.

inc-bot: :lock: Incident channel archived to thread. For follow-ups, use #incidents and link the thread.
